title: Care Plan Desk Cross-Notice: Certified Stones, Logged Inspections and the Revaluation Share
content:
For a revaluation under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes, the share taken on the figure the piece supports depends on whether the stone carries a certificate from a laboratory the programme accepts and on how many inspections have been logged, in the last 24 months, against the pieces the customer keeps covered under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans.

## The rule

Where the stone carries a certificate from a laboratory the programme accepts and two (2) or more inspections have been logged in the last twenty-four (24) months against the pieces the customer keeps covered, the share is seventy percent (70 percent); where the stone carries such a certificate but fewer than two inspections have been logged against those pieces in that time, the share is sixty-seven and a half percent (67.5 percent). Where no certificate stands on the registration, no such share applies and the share is the one the programme publishes for the current appraised value.

The certificate is the one recorded on the registration. The inspections counted are the inspection entries on the customer's care plans, of any covered piece, whose date falls within the 24 months ending on the handling date.

## Combinations

| Certificate from an accepted laboratory on the registration | Inspections logged in the last 24 months | Share |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 2 or more | 70 percent |
| yes | 0 or 1 | 67.5 percent |
| no | any number | the programme's published share for the current appraised value |

## On the boundary

- Two inspections logged, the older of them 24 months ago to the day, both count: the share is 70 percent.
- Two inspections logged, but one of them 25 months ago: only one falls within the window, and the share is 67.5 percent.
- Three inspections in the window but no certificate on the registration: the inspections do not raise the share, which stays at the programme's published figure.
